learners.robot: behaviour cloning, k-nearest neighbours (k=5) over hand-written features
learners.tutor: UCB1 bandit over hint styles + per-step error table
learners.explanations: heuristic feature attribution, fixed phrases, no model call

data: synthetic demonstrations (scripted expert at skill 0.85 with action noise), labelled synthetic; held-out seeds 7001-7060

tutor.note: simulated learners from colTutorSim's own response model; not measurements of people

preference.learner: Bradley–Terry reward model: logistic regression, no intercept, on the difference of two runs' trajectory features; L2 0.01, 500 full-batch steps from zero
preference.rater: synthetic rater: utility = 2·finished + 1·progress − 4·min(1, unsafe steps / 3) − 1.5·(steps / cap); Bradley–Terry choice at temperature 0.5
preference.keep: the top 50% of the 40 demonstrations by learned reward, fixed before any held-out seed was run; the other shares are a sensitivity sweep
preference.pairs: 200 synthetic pairs per scenario (150 to fit, 50 held out), each two runs of one seed by the scripted stand-in at two skills; labelled synthetic. A learner's consented local pairs join the fit only through rt6LocalPairs (0 here: no person's pairs exist)

pairs.rater: synthetic rater: utility = 2·finished + 1·progress − 4·min(1, unsafe steps / 3) − 1.5·(steps / cap); Bradley–Terry choice at temperature 0.5

rewardWeighted.weight: sigmoid(reward − median reward): the reward model's own probability that the demonstration is preferred over the median one, scaling every row's vote; all demonstrations kept

stepReward.rater: synthetic window rater: utility = −4·(any rule broken in the window) + 1·progress; Bradley–Terry choice at temperature 0.5

pairs.from: one window from each run of ROBOTRAIN-6's synthetic pair i (labelled synthetic)

stepReward.rule: drop a step when sigmoid(its window's reward − the median step reward) < 0.25; keep every other step of every demonstration (no run-level filter)
